## Goal
A page for Pat (72, Windows 10, a grandchild sent a file): how to open it, what the passphrase is, what the summary means, what to do if the passphrase does not work, and the two things only Pat can do (give permission, set up the email for replies). Calm, large steps, no jargon.

## Blocked: what in-house must provide first
In-house must ship the relative's side of the helper flow (double-click the file, type the passphrase, see the summary, give consent, set up the mailbox) and provide the exact labels with file:line, including the wrong-passphrase and damaged-file messages (from WO-506's typed errors). The page quotes them.

Not startable by a vendor. In-house unblocks it by changing the status line and posting a GO.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Under 500 words, reading level grade 8 or lower, steps of one action each, no step needs the keyboard shortcut or a menu name that is not on screen.
2. Every quoted label or message exists in the app, with file:line in an HTML comment.
3. Says what to do for: wrong passphrase (ask the person who sent it), damaged file (ask them to send it again), file opens in the wrong program.
4. Says plainly that Pat can stop at any time and nothing is requested from any site until Pat gives permission.
5. Forbidden-words check passes; no fear wording.
6. In-house links it from the help hub after merge (note in VENDOR_STATUS.md).

**Limits (every Grok WO, CLAUDE-G-004):** offline only. No network, credentials, git or gh, installs, or running the real app against real sites or a real mailbox; never read anything outside the repo. Fake people only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Tests pass on Windows too (`tmp_path`, `pathlib`). Check `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/`, `tests/grok/` and the in-house `tests/test_*.py` first; don't duplicate a guard.
